KV cache and prefix caching impact
oncall playbook handoff and audit logging
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-21 10:00 PT | Duration: ~65 minutes | Attendees: Priya, Marcus, Leah, Jonas, Samir, Avery, Rina, Liam; Observers: Ellen, Diego.

[00:00] Priya: okay hi everyone thanks for being here, quick agenda — finalize the thermostat thresholds, map degradation slices to capacity slabs, and decide immediate runbook edits. we only have an hour so i'll flag talk if we dig in too deep.
[00:15] Marcus: yup, quick note, we ran the 40% synthetic last night and saw about a 12% p99 spike under the current batching config, so the thermostat needs to kick earlier, maybe at 30 not 50. audio was a little messy earlier i think the transcription might drop some words.
[00:34] Leah: can you repeat that Marcus? you said thermostat at 30, why 30?
[00:40] Marcus: basically because of headroom — our p99 increases non-linearly once concurrency passes certain slab thresholds, we saw cache churn and kv evictions, so to keep latency SLO we need earlier throttling.
[00:55] Jonas: i saw that too, and there's a kernel fallback happening that makes small batches fall back to the slower kernel, that exacerbates the p99. we can tweak kernel selection heuristics but that's longer term. for launch we should avoid hitting that path.
[01:12] Priya: ok so proposal A: thermostat turns on at 30% traffic to Hosted pool and shifts to Dedicated up to 75%, beyond that we enter staged degradation - slice one, degrade non-critical routes (like embeddings bulk), slice two is model fallback to quantized variant. thoughts?
[01:32] Samir: i'm worried about bulk embeddings — customers will run large jobs at night and if we drop them they might blow up billing. can we instead throttle by token-rate not just requests?
[01:45] Marcus: yeah token-rate metric is better. we should combine token-rate and queue length to decide throttle. thermostat should be dual-signal.
[01:54] Avery: from an AE perspective we need clear messaging: when we redirect to dedicated or to quantized model, what's the UX? degraded response or a notice? we don't want customers surprised.
[02:07] Priya: agreed, Leah can we add a customer-facing note in the console and have the SDK return a specific header code for degraded responses?
[02:15] Leah: yes we can add a header x-rw-degraded: slice-name; also console banner. i'll note that.
[02:22] [02:23] Rina: on compliance, if we route to Dedicated or to Private because of region constraints we need to ensure audit logs persist and KMS usage is recorded; does our retention window change when we shift traffic? we can't accidentally short-circuit retention.
[02:39] Jonas: good call — runtime currently writes audit events to the central plane with the retention policy tied to the tenant level. when a route is promoted to dedicated it's still the same tenant so retention stays, but for private-onprem there are different concerns.
[02:55] Priya: OK so separate table — Hosted -> thermstat, Dedicated -> reserve capacity and mark as high-priority, Private -> preserve retention and no quantized fallback unless explicit permission.
[03:10] Marcus: about the staged degradation slices — propose ordering: 1) deprioritize background/async jobs (bulk embeddings, batch rerank), 2) reduce request concurrency for low-priority API keys, 3) fall back to quantized model variant, 4) fallback to smaller model family. this ordering preserves higher quality for interactive chat.
[03:33] Samir: how fast should slices apply? immediate or gradual? if immediate it might cause a thundering herd as jobs restart.
[03:40] Marcus: staggered ramp is safer. we can apply slice 1 instantly, slice 2 over 30s, slice 3 over 90s, slice 4 as last resort over 5min. those numbers are tunable.
[03:54] Priya: can we encode that in a simple state machine in the runbook + console so ops can see current slice and timers?
[04:02] Jonas: yes runtime already exposes state but the runbook needs the timers and exact thresholds. i'll add those counters.
[04:10] [04:11] Ellen (observer): quick question — what about canary pacing? if we ramp traffic and thermostat flips we might need to pause canaries.
[04:20] Priya: good point. rule: if any thermostat threshold triggers during a canary we automatically abort canary and snapshot metrics. canary should only proceed when sustained below 25% for 10m.
[04:33] Avery: do we need a special path for early enterprise customers with stricter SLAs? they might want guaranteed latency and reserved dedicated pools.
[04:42] Priya: yes enterprise reserved pools are out of thermostat; they buy isolation. but we should provide a 'protected routes' flag so customers can opt-in to preserve quality and we bill accordingly.
[04:55] Rina: security check: protected routes mean stronger logging and possibly additional KMS interactions; we must confirm key access won't add latency.
[05:04] Jonas: that will be microseconds, not major, but i'll run an isolated test.
[05:10] [05:11] Marcus: sidenote — KV cache eviction policy — at high concurrency we saw prefix cache evictions that caused upstream recompute; to avoid that we should reserve a small 'cache soft pad' on each host for inference-critical prefixes. that means slightly higher memory reserve per GPU but reduces p99.
[05:29] Leah: tradeoff is cost vs latency. product decision.
[05:34] Priya: agreed, we prefer slight cost increase for launch to protect latency. we'll revisit post-launch.
[05:40] Samir: ok, what about observability? need a per-route token-cost breakdown at the thermostat layer so we can debug which routes caused the spike.
[05:51] Marcus: we can add that metric into console and emit a trace event when thermostat engages.
[05:56] Priya: make that high priority.
[06:00] [06:05] Action recap: Marcus runs synthetic ramps at 50/80 and shares logs; Leah updates runbook and console header messaging; Jonas confirms KV cache pad config; Rina verifies audit retention for private lanes; Priya schedules tabletop.
[06:20] Leah: quick nit — runbook needs exact failure pages and play names for oncall; please list owners for each page.
[06:27] Marcus: i'll own the thermostat play, Jonas will own cache pad and kernel heuristic play, Rina owns security audit play.
[06:34] Priya: good. any other questions?
[06:38] Diego (observer): maybe we should run a small dry run with real-ish traffic from a partner to validate, can we do that before feature-freeze?
[06:45] Jonas: yes we can mirror traffic to staging but we must ensure we don't violate partner data policies.
[06:51] Priya: ok assign action: Jonas to coordinate mirror and Marcus to run ramp tests. Leah to finalize messaging and runbook. Rina to check compliance. we'll reconvene 2027-02-24 to review artifacts.
[06:58] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript: occasional dropped words and speaker tags may be approximate; timestamps are rough, every ~15-40 seconds inserted to approximate Fireflies behavior. Shared artifacts: docs/runbooks/staged-degrade-v1.pdf, console-banner-draft.md, synthetic-ramp-results-2027-02-20.zip (links in CRM ticket).
